blocks.h: From first call to water you can use
blocks.intro: Have four answers: what is in your water, which grade, how much, and what limits your site. Missing one? Send the rest. We draft, check against your budget and revise until you approve.

items.d: You send what you make and where you sell it. We return the water each product needs.
You send how much water you use a day, and your water report. We return a package size and budget range.
You agree a short user requirement specification (URS) and the proposal, so both sides sign the same scope.
We build and test the package in our shop, with you as witness, then again on your site.
We run the qualification or acceptance tests with you. Your quality person then releases the water for use.

blocks.h: Making the case inside your company
blocks.intro: Four reasons you can paste into a capital request, with the source where one applies.

items.d: In creams, liquids and drinks, water is an ingredient. Water made and tested to a written specification protects your limits and shelf life.
Health Canada's good manufacturing practice guides ask for qualified, monitored water and its test records. GUI-0001 covers drugs; GUI-0158, natural health products.
Documentation scales to your product's rules: qualification records for drug lines, an acceptance test against your specification for the rest.
Sized to the water you use each day; adding lines later is a capacity upgrade.

items.q: Our products only need potable water. Do we need this?
items.a: No, if every product's specification, monograph or recipe accepts potable water. Natural health products need potable water at minimum under GUI-0158. Cosmetics, drinks and lab water follow the standard you work to. The scope review confirms it per product.

items.q: How much water do we need?
items.a: Add up a normal day: water in your batches, equipment rinses and cleaning. Then note your busiest hour. A storage tank covers that hour, so the unit that makes the water can be smaller. Send both figures with your scope review.

items.q: Can we buy a used unit?
items.a: You can. First ask for its drawings, material certificates, test records and service history. Qualification relies on those records, so check them before you buy.

items.q: Do we need a URS before we call?
items.a: No. Tell us what you make; the scope review returns the water you need. Before an order, your requirements go into a user requirement specification (URS). Our guide shows how to write one.

items.q: How long from first call to water we can use?
items.a: Each stage's time is on our project page, counted from order and from drawing approval. Package size, your approvals and your qualification set the total.

items.q: Do we get a full pharmaceutical document pack?
items.a: No, unless your product's rules ask for one. Drug lines get qualification protocols and reports. Natural health product lines get the evidence GUI-0158 asks for: [NHP qualification scope]. Other lines get commissioning records and an acceptance test against your specification. Summary for your approver: [one-paragraph approver summary, yes or no].

A named team. Our commercial lead, an automation engineer with direct experience on pharmaceutical water systems, and a modular manufacturing and design specialist. [named project lead role] is your contact from order to handover.
